description: Width tiers for Languages — Background Language Learner F-10 Pathway, Years 9–10 band
subject: Languages — Background Language Learner

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest honest floor for the descriptor's command term at Y9-10 F-10 level. For communicating descriptors: the minimum task contexts and interaction types in which the capability is demonstrated. For understanding descriptors: the minimum range of language features, text types or cultural phenomena engaged with analytically.
width_notes.typical_width: The full descriptor scope from ACARA elaborations — what a well-taught Y9-10 background language learner F-10 class would have engaged with.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions adding new task contexts (communicating) or new phenomena (understanding). At Y9-10, formal text analysis, real community engagement, and critical intercultural reflection are primary width directions.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations for the Chinese Background Language Learner pathway (Y9-10 F-10 sequence) used as source data.

AC9LCH10C01.minimum_width: Initiate and sustain an issue-based exchange for at least six turns using at least two analytical language structures; participate in at least one formal communication context using appropriate register throughout.
AC9LCH10C01.typical_width: Initiate conversations about wider community and social issues; use analytical language to evaluate rules, policies and social questions; sustain communications in formal contexts — meetings, phone calls, official enquiries; deal with potential conflicts; write to different audiences on real-life issues; contribute to online discussions advocating positions.
wider: Produce a campaign or advocacy piece on a community issue — targeting a specific audience and using persuasive and formal structures appropriate to that audience
Compare formal communication conventions in the target language with Australian English — identify differences in register, structural conventions and opening and closing formulas
Participate in a simulation of a formal meeting or community forum where positions conflict — manage conflict productively using target language
elaborations: initiating and sustaining conversations to share issues from the wider target language community such as global warming
asking and responding to open-ended questions about promoting language learning
sustaining communications in a wide range of contexts such as meetings or phone calls
using analytical language to discuss and evaluate aspects of rules and regulations
using digital resources to maintain contact, express concerns or make enquiries
confirming understanding and requesting clarification
contributing to discussions and dealing with potential conflicts
writing to different audiences in a wide range of contexts to address real-life issues

AC9LCH10C02.minimum_width: Contribute to a group discussion with diverse perspectives using at least two negotiation strategies; contribute at least one substantive entry to a collaborative digital platform and provide justified feedback on a peer's contribution.
AC9LCH10C02.typical_width: Plan and facilitate live or online events; collaborate to create multimodal presentations for various audiences; organise authentic cultural experiences for school or community; promote inclusive cultural activities; contribute to collaborative blogs and vlogs; collect and present community data; evaluate and provide feedback on peers' contributions.
wider: Lead the organisation of a community cultural event — coordinate all planning, promotion and execution using target language, with real community participants
Collect, analyse and present community data on a cultural topic — comparing findings across different community groups and discussing what the data reveals
Create multimodal resources such as vlogs for different scenarios to help language learners at various levels
elaborations: planning and making arrangements for group activities such as itineraries for school trips
collaborating to create multimodal presentations for various audiences about the impact of social media on young people
organising an authentic cultural experience for a school or local community and collaborating with target language peers
promoting inclusive cultural activities for the local community
creating a collaborative blog about language learning experiences including tips, achievements and challenges
evaluating and providing feedback on peers' blogs using direct editing, comments or spoken feedback
creating multimodal resources such as vlogs for different scenarios to help language learners
collecting data from target language communities on various topics and presenting findings

AC9LCH10C03.minimum_width: Evaluate at least two formal target language texts using explicit credibility criteria and cite at least one source appropriately in target language; produce a formal response to a contemporary issue of at least eight sentences using at least two pieces of evidence.
AC9LCH10C03.typical_width: Evaluate key messages in contemporary target language media; analyse rhetorical questions, irony and sarcasm; access formal text types and evaluate source credibility; cite references in target language; use public speaking and debating strategies; role-play scenes demonstrating cultural knowledge; respond to literary texts with personal and analytical depth.
wider: Conduct a research task using formal target language sources — evaluate source quality, synthesise across perspectives, and present findings with citations in target language
Listen to or read a First Nations Australian author's story in English and write a reflective personal response in target language, identifying cultural perspectives and values
Analyse a contemporary issue using multiple target language sources — evaluate how different sources frame the same issue and present a synthesis that acknowledges source differences
elaborations: analysing the effectiveness of actions and evaluating against own perspectives on current issues
using various communicative strategies such as public speaking, debating or negotiating to respond to texts or topics
accessing formal text types and developing specific, formal discussions
listening to or reading First Nations Australian author's stories and presenting or writing a reflective personal response in Chinese
researching a range of resources, evaluating their validity, reliability and credibility
role-playing a modified scene from a target language movie or drama
analysing key elements of language used in successful interviews and evaluating performance
analysing the plots and personalities of key characters in a story and recreating or extending the story
reading extracts from traditional target language literature and writing reflective responses

AC9LCH10C04.minimum_width: Interpret at least two examples of puns, sarcasm or malapropisms explaining literal meaning, intended meaning and translation strategy; participate in at least one formal cultural scenario demonstrating appropriate cultural communication and justifying at least two communication decisions.
AC9LCH10C04.typical_width: Interpret puns, idioms, humour and sarcasm; explain hidden meanings in malapropisms; demonstrate politeness, respect and formality across cultural contexts; apply non-verbal communication strategies; compose multimodal bilingual texts with cultural explanation; use digital tools for emerging vocabulary; compare conventions across cultural contexts.
wider: Research a specific form of target language humour — explain how it works linguistically and culturally, why it is difficult to translate, and what strategies are most effective
Create a multimodal bilingual resource for a real community audience — evaluate cultural accuracy and accessibility with a target audience member and revise accordingly
Compare cultural communication conventions for a specific scenario (dining, business cards, welcoming) across two different target language community contexts
elaborations: applying strategies to overcome challenges in the translation of culturally unique concepts
demonstrating politeness, respect and formality in a range of cultural contexts
interpreting puns, idioms, humour or sarcasm between the target language and English
applying non-verbal and spoken communication strategies and justifying own actions and reactions
creating and developing multimodal target language resources incorporating bilingual subtitles
discussing and explaining malapropisms and translating hidden meanings
using secure online tools to understand emerging new words and applying knowledge in communication
composing multimodal bilingual texts for a range of audiences
changing informal spoken language into formal register to suit particular purposes and audiences

AC9LCH10C05.minimum_width: Produce an evaluative or persuasive text with a clear position supported by at least two pieces of evidence; create a procedural text applying correct genre conventions; create a literary text applying at least two conventions from a specific style.
AC9LCH10C05.typical_width: Produce evaluative writing; debate and write persuasive texts; create multimodal bilingual texts for community audiences; create procedural texts; write for school newspaper or magazine; produce narrative texts with logical structure; use literary style models; compose scripts and dramatic texts; create acknowledgements of country with First Nations Australians.
wider: Create a multimodal bilingual text for a real community audience — a cultural awareness training kit, community publication or school event resource — and evaluate with stakeholders
Reflect on the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place with a First Nations Australian, and present it in the target language
Create a text that applies the conventions of a specific target language literary genre — annotate the stylistic choices and explain the cultural knowledge required
elaborations: producing evaluative writing in the target language
debating or writing a text on a range of topics using persuasive language
creating multimodal bilingual texts such as a cultural awareness training information kit
reflecting on and explaining the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place with a First Nations Australian
creating a range of procedural texts in the target language
creating texts for school newspaper or magazine
identifying the morals or insight of a chosen story to produce an evaluative response
creating own imaginative stories
creating written and multimodal narrative texts using a logical structure and sequence
using models of literary styles to create texts and presenting them in multiple ways

AC9LCH10U01.minimum_width: Deliver a formal speech of at least two minutes with appropriate intonation and stress; analyse the tone patterns and rhythm of at least one text and produce an original text demonstrating at least two prosodic features identified in the analysis.
AC9LCH10U01.typical_width: Deliver authentic speech to various audiences with appropriate intonation and stress; analyse dialogues and texts for tone patterns and rhythm; develop strategies for understanding diverse regional accents; compare own speech patterns with a range of accents; perform target language works; use dictionaries and digital tools for pronunciation support.
wider: Research a specific regional accent — describe its key phonological features, find examples, and explain the comprehension strategies most useful for that variety
Create a script or spoken text specifically designed to use tonal and rhythmic patterns for effect — explain the prosodic design decisions and how they serve the communicative purpose
Compare own formal speech delivery with a published recording — identify specific prosodic differences and evaluate the effect of each
elaborations: delivering authentic speech to a range of audiences using appropriate intonation and stress
analysing a dialogue or text, identifying tone patterns and rhythm, and developing own texts with similar features
developing strategies to understand meaning when listening to diverse regional accents
comparing own Chinese speech patterns with a range of accents and creating talk show scripts
watching a range of target language performances and performing own version to the class
using appropriate intonation and pronunciation when quoting sayings from traditional literature

AC9LCH10U02.minimum_width: Use a print dictionary to look up at least three unfamiliar characters using component knowledge; produce a text demonstrating at least three complex grammatical features correctly including at least one literary or formal register feature.
AC9LCH10U02.typical_width: Use component knowledge to look up characters in print dictionaries; predict meanings of complex characters using pictographic knowledge; compare simplified and traditional character forms; apply modal and auxiliary verbs; apply complex punctuation conventions; explore literary language; discriminate correct forms and sounds of polysemous characters.
wider: Research the relationship between simplified and traditional character forms for a set of characters — explain what was simplified, the historical rationale, and discuss what is gained or lost
Investigate a polysemous character — identify all documented meanings, explain the semantic relationship between them, and create examples showing each meaning in context
Produce a text that deliberately uses a specific grammatical or literary feature for rhetorical effect — explain the choice and compare with an alternative approach
elaborations: using knowledge of components to look up new characters in print dictionaries
exploring the changes of meaning for the same characters in different contexts
predicting meanings of complex characters using knowledge of pictographs
determining the precise meanings of character morphemes by context
applying knowledge of characters and functions to compose a wide range of texts
applying knowledge of punctuation in a range of complex texts
applying knowledge of modal verbs and auxiliary verbs across text types
applying knowledge of tense in formal and informal text types
responding appropriately to sarcasm, exclamatory sentences or factual statements
identifying how sentence structures convey messages effectively
comparing known simplified characters with traditional characters and discussing differences

AC9LCH10U03.minimum_width: Identify at least three stylistic devices in a target language text using metalanguage and evaluate the effectiveness of at least one; analyse content organisation in at least two text types and compare with English conventions for at least one.
AC9LCH10U03.typical_width: Analyse linguistic features using metalanguage; analyse a range of text types and explain how language features suit different cultural contexts; compare key features in formal and informal contexts; analyse how content is structured across genres; explain how ideas are conveyed; describe genres uniquely important in target language literary tradition.
wider: Compare how argument structure and evidence presentation differ across target language and English texts — discuss what the comparison reveals about cultural epistemological conventions
Describe the purpose and features of a genre unique to the target language literary tradition, explore its origins, and create a text applying those conventions
Produce a full stylistic analysis of a target language literary text — annotating every stylistic device and evaluating the text's overall cultural and literary significance
elaborations: analysing linguistic features using metalanguage such as double negatives and parallel sentences
analysing a range of text types and explaining how different language features suit different purposes in cultural contexts
analysing and categorising cultural and linguistic elements in target language expressions
comparing key features used in formal and informal contexts in target language and English
analysing the way content is structured in a range of target language texts
analysing the use of stylistic devices in a range of written texts and evaluating their effectiveness
reading and comparing how ideas are ordered and substantiated across genres and languages
describing the purpose and features of genres uniquely important in target language literature

AC9LCH10U04.minimum_width: Evaluate how at least two cultural traditions or globalisation changes have affected communication and identity; identify at least two ways bilingual identity opens opportunities; reflect on at least one heritage or cultural connection made possible by target language knowledge.
AC9LCH10U04.typical_width: Reflect on how own identity is shaped by languages, cultures, attitudes and values; show how titles and address conventions indicate respect; indicate the impact of globalisation on cultural change; examine loan words and internet language effects on language; reflect on how non-verbal cultural behaviour affects communication; explore heritage through target language.
wider: Reflect on and explain the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place with a First Nations Australian, and discuss how this process parallels the target language community's own language-land connections
Research how a specific wave of globalisation has affected target language vocabulary and cultural practices — evaluate whether the changes strengthen or challenge cultural identity

Interview a family member about their language and cultural identity history — compare their experience of navigating between communities with own experience and discuss what has changed across generations
elaborations: reflecting on how own identity is shaped by attitudes, beliefs, values and languages used every day
showing how the use of titles indicates respect or formality compared with Australian culture
indicating the impact of globalisation on cultural change and own identity and beliefs
reflecting on and explaining the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place with a First Nations Australian
demonstrating the impact of loan words and internet language on changes in modern languages
reflecting on how non-verbal cultural behaviour such as dress codes affect communication in different cultural settings
